chests.evidence: Lobby (room 0). NoBake chest with SpawnType 1 at x=+4.1. It falls when the one Obj_EyeSwitch_A_02 above the entrance (y=109.8) is hit: EventRequestActor GerudoTrainingGround_00_FallTreasureBox references both. Link enters walking -z from the fortress (StartPos z=+11.9), so +x is his right (the Stalfos door at x=-28.4 is the left door, as in N64). The same left/right convention reproduces the N64 ice-trap pattern of the Light-trial room exactly, so it is trusted. The other lobby chest (x=-7.6) is an invisible GlassTruth chest without a Drop__DropActor (not in this list): see RC_GERUDO_TRAINING_GROUND_LOBBY_LEFT_CHEST. Contents swapped versus N64 (left blue rupee, right 10 arrows), consistent with arrows becoming rupees; SoH's CanHitEyeTargets rule still fits this chest.

Room 1 (Stalfos room, west of the lobby). Only chest there, a small key, NoBake + SpawnType 1, appearing via Gimmick_TreasureBoxAppear_Any_Fall (event GerudoTrainingGround_01_AppearTreasureBox_From00, with the room's Obj_EnemyCounter). The prefab holds 4 Enemy_Stalfos (two pairs at the same spots = waves) instead of N64's 2, hence quantity 4 (SoH's quantity is a placeholder, so this is functionally the same rule).

chests.condition: logic->CanKillEnemy(RE_WOLFOS, ED_CLOSE, true, 4, true) && logic->CanKillEnemy(RE_WHITE_WOLFOS, ED_CLOSE, true, 4, true) && logic->HasItem(RG_OPEN_CHEST)
chests.evidence: Room 3 (Wolfos room with the silver block Obj_MovableBox_A_04 at z=-97.3). Only item chest there, at (-55.1,104,-90.3), i.e. on the near side of the block. NoBake + SpawnType 1; GerudoTrainingGround_03_AppaerTreasureBox via Gimmick_TreasureBoxAppear_GerudoTrainingGround in the prefab that also holds 4 Enemy_Wolfos and 4 Enemy_Wolfos_White (pairs at identical spots = waves). N64 had Wolfos only, so the rule adds the White Wolfos. Contents 30 arrows -> blue rupee.

Room 4 (Obj_Gerudo_StoneStatue_B_01 + Obj_Gerudo_RotateFloor_A_01, lower floor y=96.3). Small key, SpawnType 1. Event GerudoTrainingGround_Room04_StoneGimmick makes it appear and opens the shutter (-2.3,106,-59.4) to the maze's upper floor; the room's Obj_EyeSwitch_A_05 is in that gimmick group. That is SoH's LOGIC_GTG_CLEARED_EYE_STATUE (bow) giving both the chest and RR_..._ABOVE_MAZE.

Room 5 (hammer room: Obj_FireTemple_HammerSlipPillar, torch slugs, fire keese). Small key sitting inside Obj_FireWall_A_01 (same position); Obj_StepSwitch_A_04 -> GerudoTrainingGround_05_DisappearFire removes the fire. Same as N64 (hammer the switch).

Room 7 (east of the lobby): Enemy_Beamos + 2 Enemy_Dinolfos in the same prefab as this key chest (NoBake, SpawnType 1, on the beamos' spot, Gimmick_TreasureBoxAppear_Any_Fall, GerudoTrainingGround_Room07_TreasureAppear). Matches SoH's rule exactly.

Room 9 (5 Obj_RupeeToken_Silver, Obj_silverRupeeCounter 2 m away, Song of Time blocks, Enemy_ShellBlade, y down to 76). Small key, NoBake, SpawnType 1 (appears on the silver-rupee count). Same as N64.

Room 10 (3 Enemy_LikeLike, behind the silver block). Invisible Obj_TBox_GlassTruth_A_01 holding a small key = N64's type-6 invisible key chest (the only key in that room in both games). Identity is solid; kept SoH's rule (lens + pass the Like Likes). Caveat: an EventRequestActor running GerudoTrainingGround_10_AppearTreasureBox also references it, so it might only appear after the room is cleared (it has no SpawnType).

Room 10. NoBake, SpawnType 1, appears through GerudoTrainingGround_10_AppearTreasureBox (Gimmick_TreasureBoxAppear_GerudoTrainingGround in the prefab with the 3 Like Likes) = a room-clear chest like N64's First and Second (both type 7). It is the only room-clear chest left, so it is First or Second; First chosen (huge rupee -> red rupee, the most valuable). Both have the same SoH rule, so the choice has no logic effect.

Room 10. Plain Obj_TBox_A_01 (bombs), no SpawnType, no links: present from the start, so it no longer needs the Like Likes killed (SoH's rule for Second). Room 10 has 5 chests against N64's 4: the GlassTruth key (Third), the A_04 trap chest (Fourth, the N64 ice trap), one room-clear chest, this one and an eye-switch chest with a Scrub Business Seed. This one is taken as N64's other room-clear chest and the seed chest as remake-new (seed chests elsewhere are mostly remake additions), but the two could be the other way round.

Room 12, left side, farthest from the door (-45.1,-16.6). Recovery heart -> blue rupee. See the First Left entry for the layout.
Room 12, right side, middle (-40.6,-27.3), between two A_04 traps. 30 arrows -> blue rupee.

Remake-new. Invisible Obj_TBox_GlassTruth_A_01 in room 13 (-52.2,100,-16.5; DefaultDungeonRoomIndex 13, 9 m from the Lullaby chest), no links, no SpawnType: always there, needs the lens. divergences.what: Ganon's Castle has 1 small key and 1 locked door (N64/SoH: 2 and 2). The light trial's first door (chest room -> triforce room) is no longer locked: it is a shutter held by the room's enemy counters, opening once the invisible enemies are dead. The only key is in a new invisible chest in the triforce room; the Invisible Enemies and Lullaby chests (N64's two keys) now hold rupees.
divergences.evidence: Obj_DoorChainLock_A_01 exists only as the pair at (-56.46,99.73,-21) on Obj_InsideGanonCastle_SwitchShutter_A_01 2559901135200913892 'SwitchShutterWithChainLock' (room 13 -> 14). The room 12 -> 13 door (17308395020688077841, x=-48) has no lock; it is in a DungeonSwitchShutterWithLockSet with Obj_EnemyCounter_A_01 290374327542697828, in the prefab with Enemy_Skulltula_Truth + 3 Enemy_Keese_Truth. The only key item in the map is the GlassTruth chest 15320975652699461295 (room 13). Obj_DoorChainLock_A_02 (room 63, 0.08,171,-7) is the boss lock on Ganondorf's door (boss key), as in SoH.
divergences.proposed_rule: dungeon.cpp: GANONS_CASTLE vanillaKeyCount 2 -> 1. Exit overrides: RR_GANONS_CASTLE_LIGHT_TRIAL_CHESTS_ROOM -> RR_GANONS_CASTLE_LIGHT_TRIAL_TRIFORCE_ROOM replaces logic->SmallKeys(SCENE_INSIDE_GANONS_CASTLE, 1) with (ctx->GetTrickOption(RT_LENS_GANON) || logic->CanUse(RG_LENS_OF_TRUTH)) && logic->CanKillEnemy(RE_BIG_SKULLTULA) && logic->CanKillEnemy(RE_KEESE, ED_CLOSE, true, 3); RR_GANONS_CASTLE_LIGHT_TRIAL_TRIFORCE_ROOM -> RR_GANONS_CASTLE_LIGHT_TRIAL_BOULDER_ROOM and RR_GANONS_CASTLE_LIGHT_TRIAL_BOULDER_ROOM -> RR_GANONS_CASTLE_LIGHT_TRIAL_TRIFORCE_ROOM replace logic->SmallKeys(SCENE_INSIDE_GANONS_CASTLE, 2) with logic->SmallKeys(SCENE_INSIDE_GANONS_CASTLE, 1). New location (remake chest 15320975652699461295) in RR_GANONS_CASTLE_LIGHT_TRIAL_TRIFORCE_ROOM: (ctx->GetTrickOption(RT_LENS_GANON) || logic->CanUse(RG_LENS_OF_TRUTH)) && logic->HasItem(RG_OPEN_CHEST). Without these, SoH would expect a second key that does not exist.
